title: WebAuthn login fixed on Windows
summary: Sign-in now works on Windows — a mismatch between the client's user-verification request and the server's stricter requirement was blocking all Windows logins.
body: If you tried to log in on Windows and were turned away, this is the fix. The server required `userVerification: "required"` but the client was sending `"preferred"`, causing a silent rejection. Both sides now agree, and Windows Hello / security-key login works as expected.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: Free self-hosted edition now enforces its own caps
summary: The 30-CISO panel and 10-industry limits for the self-hosted edition are now enforced in code, not just described on the pricing page.
body: Previously the OSS build inherited the cloud tier's wider bounds (up to 200 CISOs, unlimited industries), meaning the documented free-tier limits weren't actually applied. The caps are now hard constraints in the self-hosted build, so the pricing page and the software agree.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: PDF export now matches the full decision card
summary: Exported reports now include ranked top-3 objections, the 'what the panel almost missed' blind spot, and the Contested flag — closing the gap between the in-app view and the PDF.
body: Until now the PDF showed only a single legacy objection, while the app displayed the richer objections-led layout introduced in the Leg-2 update. The export has been brought to parity: it now renders all three ranked objections, the adversarial review's blind-spot finding, and the Contested minority flag. Single-asterisk emphasis (`*like this*`) also renders as bold in the PDF, so the report prose looks as intended.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: Native Windows installer + Apple Silicon support
summary: Príncipe now installs on Windows with a single PowerShell command, and runs natively on Apple Silicon without QEMU emulation.
body: The new `install.ps1` handles Docker Desktop and WSL2 setup automatically — no manual steps. On Apple Silicon, the installer now detects ARM64 and sets the platform flag so images build and run natively. Both installers also drop a desktop icon so you can relaunch the stack without opening a terminal.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: Windows sign-in fixed — WebAuthn verification now consistent across platforms
summary: A mismatch between the login request and server verification blocked Windows users from signing in.
body: Sign-in failed on Windows while working fine on macOS, iOS, and Android. The root cause was a mismatch: the login flow requested `userVerification: "preferred"` but the server enforced `"required"`, so Windows Hello credentials were silently rejected. Both sides now agree on `"required"`, and Windows login works as expected.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: Self-hosted caps are now enforced in code
summary: The free self-hosted edition now hard-limits panels to 30 CISOs and industries to 10, matching the published pricing.
body: Previously the OSS build inherited a wider brand clamp and the 30-CISO / 10-industry limits were stated in docs but not enforced at runtime. Those caps are now checked in code, so the self-hosted edition behaves exactly as described on the pricing page. Cloud and licensed tiers are unaffected.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: PDF export now matches the full objections card

title: Two medium security findings closed — XSS in news feed and DNS-rebinding SSRF
summary: News-body content is now sanitized with DOMPurify, and the SSRF guard closes a DNS-rebinding bypass by pinning TCP connections to the pre-validated IP.
body: The NewsBell panel previously rendered news content without sanitization, allowing potential XSS via crafted news items; it now runs DOMPurify with hardened anchor attributes. A separate DNS-rebinding path let an attacker bypass the SSRF IP-validation check by racing a DNS response after validation; outbound fetch now pins the TCP connect to the IP resolved at validation time via an undici dispatcher, closing the race window. Both findings came from an external security audit.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.
